c1.mp3: Your own GLP-1 is gone almost as fast as it arrives. An enzyme in your blood cuts it in about two minutes. So by the time it could be useful as a medicine, it has already been taken apart. That was the wall for years. You cannot inject something that disappears before it works. What changed was not a better idea about the hormone. What changed was finding a version of it that the enzyme could not cut.
c2.mp3: People call it food noise. It is not hunger. Hunger comes and goes, and you can answer it. This was a conversation that never stopped. What is in the kitchen? What I ate yesterday? What I am allowed to have? What that makes me? Two weeks in, I noticed I had walked past the kitchen without the conversation starting. That is the part nobody warned me about. Not the wait, the quiet.
c3.mp3: About 327 people came off the drug and were followed for a year. On average, about two-thirds of the weight they had lost came back. I want to be careful about how that gets read. It does not mean the treatment failed, and it does not mean those people failed. It means the drug was doing something continuously, and when it stopped, the thing it was doing stopped too. Blood pressure and cholesterol drifted back the same way, and a year later that group was still lighter than when they started. Both things are true at once.
